figures.name: r47_current_state_transfer
figures.title: R47: current-state gain in-domain, no established history gain
figures.caption: Lines are recorded adjusted 97.5% patient-bootstrap intervals. Current measured anatomy and the retrospectively supplied interval improve the in-domain distributional score against persistence. The history increment is unresolved and the current-state advantage does not transfer. Panels use independent axis limits. Source results average two repeated nested partitions; locked source models supply developmental transfer predictions.

figures.name: r49_pretraining_scores
figures.title: R49: matched pretraining improves overlap, absolute Dice stays low
figures.caption: Points are means of patient-uniform scores over two fitted seeds on 60 visits from 13 reused LUMIERE scoring patients. No arm-wise uncertainty is supplied here. Architecture, supervision, patient draws, and selection opportunities are matched. Dice is unitless with 1 indicating perfect overlap. The next figure gives the paired uncertainty and volume-retention criterion.

figures.name: r49_pretraining_contrasts
figures.title: R49: paired evidence for an initialization benefit
figures.caption: Lines are adjusted 97.5% patient-bootstrap intervals over 13 scoring patients. Both seeds favor pretraining for Dice. The volume interval crosses zero but its upper limit passes the specified +0.05 retention allowance. This supports initialization under the matched recipe, not clinical utility or temporal understanding. Panels have different units.

figures.name: r50_r51_clinical_objectives
figures.title: R50/R51: no accepted primary JEPA gain across the three recipes
figures.caption: Lines are family-three adjusted 98.33% patient-bootstrap intervals for observed four-class response log loss on 10 reused scoring patients. Versions change bundled training choices and are not a controlled single-factor ablation. v3 recovers fitting readiness; v1 and v2 retain their readiness limitations. Independent panel scales preserve visible uncertainty. The observed-response task is not future forecasting.

figures.name: r52_token_interface
figures.title: R52: a token-interface replacement was not established
figures.caption: The candidate is the compact CNN, so all signs are CNN minus BrainIAC. Lines are family-three adjusted 98.33% patient-bootstrap intervals on 13 reused LUMIERE patients. Both encoders use the same 216 by 64 token interface and fresh readouts. Mean Dice is about 0.0666 for both. The figure does not identify whether information was lost in the backbone, interface, or readout.

figures.name: r53_image_prediction
figures.title: R53: small completion gain, no useful image-forecast gain
figures.caption: Lines are family-five adjusted 99% patient-bootstrap intervals. Completion uses 13 scoring patients and forecasting uses 10. Errors are in standardized image-intensity units, not physical tissue units. The small completion improvement misses the fixed useful-gain criterion. Separate panel scales avoid hiding the near-zero forecast contrasts.

figures.name: r56_r57_regional_context
figures.title: Regional context helps one current-state endpoint
figures.caption: R56 uses ordinary 95% patient-bootstrap intervals; R57 uses family-three adjusted 98.33% intervals. Both score 10 reused patients. R56 scores all regions; R57's primary endpoint scores nonempty regions. Context improves R57 against self-only messages, but adjacency and history increments remain unresolved. These coarse log-count targets predate R60's source-volume correction and require separate confirmation. Panels have different endpoints.

figures.name: r58_future_features
figures.title: R58: future-feature alignment did not improve anatomical forecasting
figures.caption: Lines are family-three adjusted 98.33% patient-bootstrap intervals on eight reused scoring patients. Current automated measurements are supplied at inference; future inputs are excluded. Teacher and encoder are frozen. Targets are the coarse regional log-count measurements later questioned by R59 and corrected in R60.

figures.name: r48_fitting_duration
figures.title: R48: the short fitting check stopped too early
figures.caption: Recorded checkpoints on the same two fitting examples. Lines connect measurements, with no uncertainty band or interpolated observations. Both arms pass the full original fitting criterion by 512 updates. This diagnoses optimization duration; it is not held-out generalization or evidence of pretrained superiority. Dice is unitless.

figures.name: r54_individual_fitting
figures.title: R54: fitting remains weak even on two examples
figures.caption: Points are the two examples' relative MAE reductions against their best image control, multiplied by 100. Shape and color identify examples; they are not bootstrap samples or error bars. The best control can differ between completion and forecasting examples. Frozen and trainable describe the MRI encoder. None meets the substantial-fit criterion. These are fitting-only diagnostics, not held-out performance.

figures.name: r55_decoder_fitting
figures.title: R55: bypassing the MRI encoder did not resolve image fidelity
figures.caption: Recorded mean scores on two current fitting images, in standardized intensity units. Codes-only and codes-plus-decoder runs fit target-specific spatial codes. MRI continuation uses the matched additional duration. Lines connect recorded checkpoints; no uncertainty is supplied. None met the full individual-image fitting criterion. These curves do not measure forecasting or generalization. R54's preceding fitting diagnosis also failed its substantial-fit criterion.

figures.name: r59_coarse_measured_history
figures.title: R59: measured-history comparison before target correction
figures.caption: Lines are family-two adjusted 97.5% patient-bootstrap intervals on 30 history pairs from eight reused patients. This comparison uses the old coarse-grid log-count targets. R59's separate inspection of six deliberately selected examples found erased burden and a change-direction disagreement; those examples cannot estimate prevalence. R60 quantifies the defect and R61 repeats the comparison with source-volume targets. Do not compare absolute R59 and R61 errors as a single-factor sampling correction: the logarithm's volume units also changed.

figures.name: r60_target_correction
figures.title: R60: coarse sampling erased burden and reversed some changes
figures.caption: Bars show endpoint-pooled counts divided by all compared region-compartment cells in each partition. Labels give numerator/denominator; these are not percentages among positive cells or patient-uniform forecast scores. No sampling uncertainty is supplied. Source-volume aggregation conserves physical volume. This is a target diagnostic across 322 visits, not a model comparison or proof of biological mask accuracy.

figures.name: r61_r62_measured_history
figures.title: Corrected measured history still loses to persistence
figures.caption: Points show patient-uniform regional MAE of log(1 + volume in mL), not raw mL. Both earlier and current measurements are supplied to history regressions. Persistence copies current measured burden. Trend selects zero and coincides with persistence. No arm-wise uncertainty is supplied. Panels use independent scales and different anatomical tasks: three automated compartments in R61, four reviewed-mask compartments including cavity in R62. Absolute errors are not a cross-cohort leaderboard. All scoring patients are development evidence; MU's forty reserved patients remain unopened.

figures.name: r61_r62_history_intervals
figures.title: Small history increments do not beat persistence
figures.caption: Lines are family-two adjusted 97.5% paired patient-bootstrap intervals. R61's history-minus-current interval excludes zero but the gain misses the fixed 5% practical threshold. R62's corresponding interval crosses zero. Both history-minus-persistence intervals favor persistence. Panels have independent scales and different compartment definitions; do not pool their estimates.

figures.name: r61_r62_error_strata
figures.title: Learned corrections help changed cells but add empty-cell error
figures.caption: Descriptive patient-uniform error strata for the same R61 and R62 scoring cohorts. Empty and nonempty refer to the future target; changed cells exceed the fixed 0.1 log1p-mL absolute-change threshold. Strata overlap and must not be added. No stratum-specific intervals are supplied. Each panel has its own scale. The overall criterion still favors persistence.

figures.name: r62_development_cohort
figures.title: MU development allocation and history eligibility
figures.caption: Assigned and history-eligible patient counts are overlapping categories, not stacked groups. The eligible partitions provide 107, 47, and 33 triples respectively. Metadata anomalies and missing released files exclude affected comparisons. Forty separately reserved patients remain unopened and are not represented by image or mask measurements in this plot.
